newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: CRICKET-DEAL PROPOSED TO GET SOHAIL BAN LIFTED.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-DEAL PROPOSED TO GET SOHAIL BAN LIFTED.

text.p: A deal has been proposed to allow Pakistan opener Aamir Sohail's two-year ban from domestic and international cricket to be lifted if he apologises to the game's ruling body in his country.

A Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) spokesman, quoted by the official APP news agency, said on Tuesday the deal was suggested by Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif's adviser on sports and culture Mushahid Hussain at the weekend.
Sohail's suspension was imposed last month for alleged violation of the PCB code of conduct.
"Mushahid proposed that while Sohail will render a written apology for his acts of misbehaviour, the PCB should, in turn, lift the two years' ban...," spokesman Rafi Nasim said.
"Aamir Sohail is welcome to submit his letter of apology which will be placed before the PCB council for consideration," he said, adding that the apology had not yet been received.
A PCB disciplinary committee announced the ban on April 16 after Sohail was initially suspended for a month over a row with board chief executive Majid Khan during a domestic one-day game.
The three-man committee found Sohail guilty of breaching the code of conduct by levelling what it called baseless charges of match-fixing and betting against some national team members.
Sohail, who has played 34 tests, scoring 2,103 runs at an average of 35.64, has 60 days from the date of the committee's decision to appeal for a review the ban.
